This message comes from Schwab.
Investing with Schwab is like a hike with endless trails.
Go solo with self-directed investing,
take stops along the way with trading,

Whatever trails you take,
you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington,
I'm Linda Kenyon.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio is defending
President Trump's decision to start the war against Iran,
even though it likely led to Republican losses
in the midterm elections.
The President of the United States identified
a very real threat to this country
that's existed for a very long period of time,
and he addressed it.
And he addressed it even though oftentimes
the right thing to do for the country,
confronting difficult challenges
for the security of our country,
doing it isn't necessarily popular, but necessary.
Rubio says the war was necessary to stop Iran
from getting a nuclear weapon.
Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont says the war
against Iran was not necessary.
I hope my Republican colleagues understand
that the American people are sick and tired
of this unconstitutional and illegal war,
which has not only raised prices in America,
but has killed 19 American service members
and thousands of people in Iran,
innocent men, women, and children.
On CNN's State of the Union,
Sanders said the incoming Democratic majority
must defund the Iran war.
NVIDIA is investigating an alleged relationship
between its CEO and a Chinese businesswoman
who is accused of spying for China,
and PR's Rebecca Hersher reports.
The statement by NVIDIA's board of directors
cites recent reporting by the New York Times,
which alleges that the CEO of NVIDIA,
Jensen Huang, had a close relationship
with a woman named Alice Huang.
The two are not related.
Times reporter Anna Swanson discussed the reporting
on NPR technology podcast, Machine Gods.
So Alice Huang is a Chinese national.
She's a Chinese businesswoman who had something
of kind of a mysterious and meteoric rise.
The reporting by the Times suggests
Huang may have helped China get around U.S. limits
on exports of powerful AI chips.
Republican lawmakers have asked NVIDIA's CEO
to appear before Congress to address the allegations.
Rebecca Hersher, NPR News.
The floodwaters have receded across Southwest Colorado.
At least 700 homes in Archuleta County have been affected.
Colorado Public Radio Stena Sieg reports.
Many are around the small town of Pagosa Springs,
where the San Juan River nearly hit
a historic high November 1st,
more than four feet above major flood stage.
Local pastor John Duncan with Centerpoint Church
has been helping residents.
He says they're resilient, but many are overwhelmed.
It's just heartbreaking as you watch the memories
of your children and the treasures
that you've kept floating around
in your house completely ruined.
Duncan is hosting dozens of out-of-town church members
helping clean up the devastation.
For NPR News, I'm Stena Sieg in Grand Junction, Colorado.
You're listening to NPR.
The U.S., U.K., Canada, and seven other governments
have issued a joint statement
calling Hong Kong's sentencing
of prominent democracy activist Joshua Wong unjust.
Hong Kong's government calls that statement
a distortion of the facts.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reports from Beijing.
Hong Kong's government says Wong was convicted
of foreign collusion based on evidence
and denies it was targeting individuals
for political expression or participation.
But the sentencing for Wong came just as he was nearing
the end of another prison term.
It was also a conviction
under the Beijing-imposed national security law.
The U.S., along with nine other governments,
says the law has been used
to also target other political activists.
In a joint statement, they urged Hong Kong
to honor the rights and freedoms
guaranteed under an agreement
when the British handed Hong Kong back to China in 1997.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
It was a big weekend at the movies.
Ticket sales were brisk for the movie "Godzilla Minus Zero,"
which topped the box office charts.
That film brought in more than $31 million
in sales across the country.
The movie easily outpaced
the Warner Brothers animated film "The Cat in the Hat."
That film brought in more than $20 million.
Coming in third place was the movie "Drummer Boy,"
which earned $9.3 million during its opening weekend.
Oscar-contending "Wild Horse Nine" had a promising opening,
bringing in $6 million at the box office.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
